title: GST Decoded chapter navigation
summary: Turn an 18-chapter scrolling course into a navigable learning journey without disrupting its cinematic reading experience.

brief.outcome: Let readers see where they are, jump between chapters, and return to the same chapter reliably on desktop and mobile.
users: First-time readers moving through the course sequentially
Returning readers revisiting a specific GST topic
constraints: Preserve the existing React, TypeScript, Vite, GSAP, and Framer Motion stack
Do not obscure chapter content or compete with the storytelling
Respect keyboard navigation and reduced-motion preferences

requirements.text: Keep the active chapter synchronized while the reader scrolls through all 18 chapters.
requirements.proof: The repository already centralizes chapter metadata and observes chapter sections through useChapterInView.

requirements.text: Encode chapter selection in the URL so deep links and browser history remain useful.
Expose a compact mobile chapter picker and a persistent desktop rail with the same interaction model.

architecture.overview: Keep chapterMeta as the source of truth, add a small navigation controller that reconciles viewport state with the URL, and let desktop and mobile views consume the same controller rather than duplicating behavior.

components.name: Chapter navigation controller
components.responsibility: Resolve initial deep links, update the active chapter, and prevent URL-scroll feedback loops.
components.failure_boundary: An invalid chapter parameter falls back to the first chapter without breaking render.

components.name: Desktop chapter rail
components.responsibility: Show location, chapter titles, completion context, and direct navigation without covering course content.

components.name: Mobile chapter sheet
components.responsibility: Offer the same chapter map in a touch-friendly progressive disclosure pattern.

decisions: Use the existing chapter metadata instead of introducing a second navigation registry.
Use replaceState during passive scrolling and pushState only for explicit chapter jumps.
Keep motion decorative; navigation state must remain correct when motion is disabled.

acceptance_criteria.text: Opening a valid chapter deep link scrolls to that chapter and marks it active.
Scrolling across chapter boundaries updates the URL without filling browser history with passive updates.
Every navigation control is keyboard reachable, visibly focused, and labeled with chapter number and title.
At 390px width, the course has no horizontal overflow and the chapter picker does not cover reading content when closed.

tasks.title: Unify URL and viewport chapter state
tasks.verification: Unit tests for initial URL, invalid URL, passive scroll, and explicit jump behavior.

tasks.title: Refine desktop and mobile navigation surfaces
tasks.verification: Keyboard walkthrough and Playwright checks at desktop and 390px viewports.

tasks.title: Run adversarial navigation verification
tasks.verification: Reload, back/forward, rapid chapter jumps, reduced motion, and invalid deep-link cases.

critiques.finding: A large always-open mobile table of contents would interrupt the course more than it helps.
critiques.disposition: Use a compact current-chapter trigger and reveal the full list only on demand.

critiques.finding: Two independent active-chapter states would drift during smooth scrolling and browser navigation.
critiques.disposition: Centralize reconciliation in one controller consumed by both responsive surfaces.

decisions.title: Preserve the course as one continuous document
decisions.rationale: The cinematic narrative depends on uninterrupted scrolling; navigation should orient readers rather than turn chapters into separate routes.

verification.name: Repository inspection
verification.evidence: Inspected clean commit 671c35e: 18 chapter modules, chapterMeta, ChapterNav, useChapterInView, and scrollIntoView are present.

verification.name: Proposed behavior
verification.evidence: This report is the implementation contract; no GST Decoded source files were changed.

evidence.name: Read-only repository analysis
evidence.detail: The demo was generated against the public GST Decoded repository without modifying its worktree.

gaps: The proposed interaction still requires implementation and browser-level verification in GST Decoded.
